info.desc: End of the Century is the fifth studio album by the American punk rock band Ramones, recorded on May 7, 1979 and released on February 4, 1980, through Sire Records. The album was the band's first produced by Phil Spector, though he had offered the band his assistance earlier in their career. With Spector fully producing the album, it was the first release that excluded original member Tommy Ramone, who in 1978 left the band but produced their previous album Road to Ruin. Spector used more advanced standards of engineering, such as high-quality overdubbing and echo chambers. These methods caused .

podcast.body: This album was produced by Phil Spector, a legendary but volatile producer, in a bid to expand the Ramones' fanbase. The recording sessions were notoriously difficult, with Spector's perfectionism and temper leading to extreme situations, including allegedly holding Joey and Dee Dee Ramone at gunpoint. The album, which took nearly a year to record and months to remix, was released in winter 1980, earned respectable reviews and better-than-average sales for the band, reaching their highest placement ever on the Billboard album chart at number 44. It also featured a cover of The Ronettes' "Baby I Love You" sung by Joey Ramone and Dee Dee Ramone's "Chinese Rock," an ode to his heroin addiction. "When the cursed album finally came out in the winter of 1980... end of the century earned respectable reviews and better than average sales for the Ramones."
